label: Displacement Convexity I
notes: This chapter, printed pages 435 to 448, asks which functionals of a probability measure stay convex when we move along Wasserstein geodesics rather than straight mixtures. Displacement interpolation transports mass; the internal energy then traces a convex profile that quietly encodes the curvature of the underlying space.

label: Two Ways to Interpolate
notes: Linear interpolation averages two densities pointwise, so a single peak typically splits into two. Displacement interpolation instead slides mass along optimal geodesics, producing one travelling bump. The internal energy behaves very differently on these two paths, and that contrast is the engine of the whole chapter.

label: McCann Displacement Interpolation
notes: McCann's theorem builds the geodesic mu_t by pushing the source forward under the map that interpolates the optimal transport. Each particle travels a straight Euclidean segment at constant speed. The resulting curve of measures is the unique constant-speed Wasserstein geodesic between its endpoints in flat space.

label: Internal Energy Functionals
notes: Internal energy integrates a nonlinearity u of the density against the reference volume. Boltzmann entropy uses u of r equal to r log r; Renyi-type energies use power laws. These functionals measure concentration, and their convexity along displacement is the property we want to characterise sharply.

label: The Definition of Displacement Convexity
notes: A functional is displacement convex when its restriction to every Wasserstein geodesic is a convex function of the interpolation parameter. Lambda-convexity strengthens this with a quadratic modulus. This is convexity along the right paths, not along linear mixtures, and that distinction is everything here.

label: McCann's Condition on the Nonlinearity
notes: McCann found the exact algebraic test in flat n-dimensional space. Rewrite the nonlinearity through the map r maps to r to the N times u of r to the minus N, where N is the dimension. If this transformed function is convex and nonincreasing, the internal energy is displacement convex for every pair of measures.

label: Why the Substitution Appears
notes: Along a geodesic the Jacobian of the transport map controls how volume dilates. Writing the density as mass over a determinant turns the integral into a function of that determinant raised to the power one over N. The convexity of the pressure profile in this variable is exactly McCann's condition.

label: The Convex Profile in Action
notes: Sampling the entropy along the displacement geodesic produces a curve that bows downward, sitting on or below its chord. Sampling it along the linear mixture produces a curve that bulges upward and violates the inequality. The toy computation in the notebook makes this convexity residual numerically visible.

label: Entropy and Renyi Examples
notes: Boltzmann entropy passes McCann's test in every dimension, so it is displacement convex in flat space. The Renyi entropies given by power-law nonlinearities are displacement convex precisely when their exponent lies above the dimensional threshold one minus one over n. Below it convexity can fail.

label: The Headline Link to Ricci
notes: On a manifold the flat criterion is no longer enough. Displacement convexity of the Boltzmann entropy along Wasserstein geodesics becomes equivalent to nonnegative Ricci curvature. Lower Ricci bounds translate into lambda-convexity moduli, opening the synthetic Lott-Sturm-Villani definition of curvature for metric measure spaces.

label: Reading Curvature from a Curve
notes: The chapter's payoff is a dictionary: a purely analytic convexity statement about entropy along transport geodesics encodes a purely geometric statement about Ricci curvature. We close by checking that the discrete entropy curve in the notebook satisfies its convexity residual, confirming the inequality is real.
